observations: Photo 0: Blue cast-body gear reducer with a yellow output shaft/coupling area; mounted on a rectangular base/foot.
Photo 1: Side view shows the reducer body, flange/base, and the output shaft end; no visible nameplate/ratings.
Photo 2: Opposite side view shows the housing and mounting feet; no visible model/serial plate.

identity.kind: gear reducer (cast body) for industrial drive

claims.claim: Gear reducer 15 to 20hp cast bodies types
claims.evidence: No visible nameplate, rating plate, or markings in photos 0-2 to confirm the 15–20hp suitability or exact type.

risks.risk: Unknown gear ratio/output speed and torque rating (critical for matching to the motor and load). Photos don’t show ratio markings.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the nameplate/label showing gear ratio (i), output speed (rpm), and torque (Nm) OR the exact model number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used gear reducer with unknown ratio: worst-case treated as not confirmed for the stated hp/load.

risks.risk: Unknown input/output shaft sizes and coupling compatibility (may not fit the motor or driven equipment).
risks.proof: Measure and photograph: input shaft diameter/length and output shaft diameter/length with a ruler/caliper; also show any keyway.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring possible shaft/coupling adaptation.

risks.risk: Condition/working status not proven (could be worn, noisy, leaking, or seized). Photos only show appearance.
risks.proof: Short video of it running under load (or at least free-run) showing smooth rotation and no abnormal noise/leakage.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: needs service/overhaul).

risks.risk: Oil condition/leakage and seal health not verifiable from photos.
risks.proof: Photo of oil level/condition (if sight glass) and close-up of seals/gaskets; plus wipe test showing no fresh leaks after running.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may need oil/seal replacement.

risks.risk: Unclear whether it is single reducer or multi-stage and whether it matches the seller’s 'type' wording.
risks.proof: Nameplate/model photo and a shot showing the internal stage layout if visible on the housing/cover.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the simplest generic cast-body reducer without confirmed stage/type.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the nameplate/serial/model plate (must be readable) showing: model, gear ratio, input/output rpm, and mounting type.
Video of the reducer running (free-run and ideally under load) with sound/noise check and no leakage.
Measurements/photos of input and output shaft diameters, keyway size, and shaft length (with a ruler/caliper).
Photo of any oil level/sight glass and close-ups of seals/gaskets; confirm oil type and whether it leaks.
response.reason: The photos show a cast-body gear reducer, but there is no readable model/nameplate or confirmed ratio/speed/shaft specs, and working condition is not proven—so a worst-case price cannot be set confidently without the key identification and proof.
